SAMSUNG R&D Bangalore 
Siddhesh Bandgar  TYBTECH CS  2018-22 
 
Samsung was the first company that visited our campus after MST. Total 3 
rounds were conducted (1 coding + 2 interview). There was no HR round. There 
was a 2 days gap between the online coding test and the interviews. 
Round 1: Online Assessment 
Round 1 consisted of 3 coding questions. Time given was 70 minutes. Coding test 
was conducted on Cocubes platform. Use of STL was allowed. There were 
various sets of questions. My questions were as follows: 
1. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/program-for-armstrong-numbers/ 
(Efficient approach was needed) (2 marks) 
2. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sum-of-cousins-of-a-given-node-in-a-binar
y-tree/​ (3 marks) 
3. Find the sum of all the left leaf nodes of the binary tree having right 
sibling. (3 marks) 
Only basic test cases were visible during the test. It was explicitly mentioned 
that optimized solutions will be given more preference. Try to optimize your 
solutions as much as possible. Prepare trees well for clearing the first round of 
Samsung. 
Total 9 people were selected for the second round. Luckily, I was one of them. 
 
 
 
1

Round 2: Technical Interview 
Our interviews were scheduled 2 days after the online assessment. Interviews 
started quite late at around 5:30 in the evening.  
Interviewer was friendly. He started with asking about how Covid has impacted 
my life.  
He then asked a few questions about my projects mentioned in my resume. For 
eg. What is your project? What tech stack is used? Why did you use that tech 
stack? What was your role in the project? 
He then started with coding questions which are as follows: 
1. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/find-two-rectangles-overlap/  
2. Implement a queue using two stacks. 
3. What is preorder, postorder inorder traversals? He then told me to give all 
three traversals of the binary tree given by him. Then, he asked about the 
real life use of postorder traversal. On which I told him how the compiler 
converts mathematical expressions to postfix expressions and evaluates 
them. He then asked me the code for postfix expression evaluation. 
4. How to reverse a linked list? 
He then asked if I had some questions for him. I asked about my feedback and 
he told me that he was quite happy with my knowledge of data structures and 
algorithms. I asked a few company related questions and then the interview 
ended.  
Interview went for about 50-60mins. 
 
 
 
2

Round 3: Technical Interview 
Round 3 started at around 7 in the evening. 
Interviewer was in the Samsung office and was ready to leave for home. So he 
looked in quite a hurry. He asked me to introduce myself. After that he asked 
about my projects and asked some standard project related questions. If you 
have web development project related to seat booking in your resume, then 
always be prepared for 2 questions: 
1. If two users are accessing your web page simultaneously, and select the 
same seat how would you resolve that issue? 
2. If many people are accessing your website, how would you manage it 
efficiently? 
He then started with coding questions which are as follows: 
1. We have been given call records of a certain day at a call centre i.e the 
start time and end time of each call is given. Considering that calls occur 
at the same time every day, we have to find the minimum number of 
operators needed such that no call is left unattended and no operator is 
sitting idle. It is similar to the​ ​Number of Platforms needed​ problem. 
2. Then he asked a small puzzle. We have 3 boxes. One contains red balls 
,one contains green balls, and the third one contains both color balls. They 
all have labels on top stating the colour of the balls inside it namely ‘Red’, 
‘Green’, ‘Mixed’. It is known that all the labels are wrongly placed. How 
many minimum numbers of balls need to be taken out to find the right 
label and the right box associated with it. 
 
3

https://www.glassdoor.co.in/Interview/You-re-given-three-boxes-with-red-
balls-in-the-first-one-blue-in-the-second-and-red-and-blue-both-in-the-thir
d-The-boxes-QTN_566043.htm 
3. We are given an array containing 1s and 0s. Segregate all 1s on the right 
side and 0s on the left side or vice versa. There are many approaches to 
this problem. I started with the most obvious approach and then went on 
to an optimized one. 
4. He asked me if I know about Trie data structure. He asked what it is, what 
it is used for, and how it is implemented. He then asked if we have a 
phone book containing various names, how will you efficiently insert 
names in it to reduce the lookup time. Then he asked about the time and 
space complexity of it. 
5. We are given two linked lists and pointers to their head. Find if these 
linked lists merge. 
He then asked if I had any questions for him and the interview ended.  
Results were declared on the same day at around 11pm. 6 people, including me, 
were selected for a 2 months internship. 
Be confident in what you are answering. Even if you do not know the answer, 
just tell the interviewer your approach and he’ll surely give you a hint. Even after 
that if you didn’t get the answer, do not panic. Interviewer judges you based on 
how you approach the solution, even if you don't reach the final step. 
All the best!
